title: Cold rebuild: Compose a validator
summary: Rebuild Compose a validator from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Compose a validator** in *Higher-Order Functions*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: const twice = (f: (n: number) => number) => (n: number) => f(f(n));

steps.title: Rebuild Compose a validator cold
prompt: A rule is `(value: string) => string | null`: it returns an error message, or `null` when the value is fine.
Write `combine(...rules)` that returns one rule which runs every rule and returns the **first** error, or `null` if all pass. Then the tests use it with these rules (already written in the starter):
const maxLen = (n: number) => (v: string) => (v.length <= n ? null : `max ${n} characters`);
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
const maxLen = (n: number): Rule => v => (v.length <= n ? null : `max ${n} characters`);
